title: Bayesian Model Averaging for Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Agent Orchestration
research_question: Can Bayesian model averaging over multiple workflow-performance models improve task routing and decomposition decisions in multi-agent systems compared with selecting a single orchestration model?
hypothesis: In agentic workflow optimization, single-model orchestration becomes overconfident under shifting task and environment conditions; averaging across plausible workflow models will reduce unnecessary adaptations and improve end-to-end task success and efficiency.
motivation: The knowledge base highlights a specific gap: model-selection uncertainty is explicitly identified as under-addressed in self-adaptive systems, where choosing one best model can produce overconfident predictions, missed adaptations, and unnecessary adaptations. This idea appears well-developed for MAPE-K self-adaptive systems but not yet translated into agentic workflow orchestration, where planners must route tasks among multiple agents under nonstationary conditions. Applying Bayesian model averaging to orchestration is a promising cross-domain direction because the underlying failure mode is structurally similar: both settings must adapt online while reasoning over uncertain performance models.
